title: The marriage supper (Revelation 19)
hook: blessed are those called to the marriage supper of the Lamb

segments.voice: Yesterday, Babylon fell, and its cargo list ended with people. Your line was bodies and souls. What did you buy more fairly? Day one thousand three hundred nine.

Smoke is still rising from Babylon. And then a sound comes over it, and John describes it three ways at once: like a great crowd, like rushing water, like thunder. And what the crowd is shouting isn't a war cry. It's a word you may have sung yourself: "Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth." Then the crowd says why they're so happy. Not a battle. A wedding. "The marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready." After all the seals and trumpets and bowls and beasts, Revelation's next great scene of joy is a party. Today's word is that party: the marriage supper.

First, two women. Yesterday's Babylon was a woman in purple and scarlet, decked with gold. Today's bride wears something plainer. The text says: "to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints." Notice the word granted. The verse before says she made herself ready; this one says the linen was given to her. Churches weigh those two lines differently. Christian tradition reads the bride as the people of God, the church, married to the Lamb. Second, the invitation. An angel tells John to write: "Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb." Jesus told stories about this feast. In Matthew, "The kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain king, which made a marriage for his son," and the invitations go out to the streets. In John's Gospel, the beginning of his signs was at a wedding in Cana, when the wine ran out. His signs begin at a wedding, and near the end of Revelation the story arrives at one. Third, John gets it wrong. Overwhelmed, he falls at the angel's feet to worship. The angel stops him: "See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant." Worship God. Even the angel is a fellow servant. Fourth, the shape of Christian hope here. It isn't only escape, or rest, or a verdict. It's a table, a meal with people you love, the kind of joy that has music and too much food. Some Christians at communion speak of tasting that feast ahead of time; churches understand the meal differently, and some set the table with this hope in view.
screen: `A BRIDE IN LINEN, GIVEN TO HER.`
`EVEN THE ANGEL IS A FELLOW SERVANT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: plan a festive table. Settle, and breathe. Think of your next meal with someone, tonight or this week. What would make it feel like a feast? Not expensive. A candle. A cloth on the table. Flowers from outside. Phones put away. Someone you'd love to invite who rarely gets invited. Picture the table set, the people around it, the noise. If you pray, you can give thanks for it ahead of time. If you don't, just enjoy picturing it. The bell holds the time.
The marriage supper. In Revelation nineteen, the wedding feast of the Lamb and his bride, and the blessing on everyone called to it.

Your line: the wedding feast. This week ran from two witnesses in the street, past a dragon, beasts, a harvest, a song and a fallen city, to a wedding. Today, set one table a little more festively, and invite someone to it. Day one thousand three hundred nine.

howItsDone: In some churches, the words of Revelation 19:9 are said at communion, just before people come to the table, and Christian weddings and feast-day meals are described by some as a foretaste of the wedding feast of the Lamb.

notes: Day 1309 is a week end: the carry looks back over days 1303–1309.
'The beginning of his signs was at a wedding in Cana' follows John 2:11 ('This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee').
'Christians read the bride as the people of God, the church' is stated broadly; confirm acceptable for this path.

Communion line: 'churches understand the meal differently, but many set the table with this hope in view' and howItsDone says Revelation 19:9 is said at communion 'in some churches' (e.g., the Catholic Mass's 'Blessed are those called to the supper of the Lamb'). Confirm.

Editor pass: removed 'the Bible's last great scene of joy' (Rev 21 follows); 'Christians read the bride' made 'Christian tradition'; angel 'a guest' changed to 'a fellow servant' per 19:10; communion line limited to 'some Christians'. The earlier note quoting 'many set the table' is outdated: the script says 'some'.

Audit 2026-10-02: SERIOUS: teach head said 'EVEN THE ANGEL IS A GUEST', contradicting 19:10 (fellowservant); fixed. 'In Revelation the whole story ends at one [wedding]' was wrong (chs 20–22 follow); fixed. 'Her dress is a gift' and the 'earned' myth took a side on grace and works; now sets 19:7 (made herself ready) beside 19:8 (granted) without ranking. Keeper: confirm.
